summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — XYZ +7%, TTWO +6%, ABNB +5%, MRNA +4%, WDC +4%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (CBOE -9%, MPWR -9%, INTC -8%, LITE -8%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: CBOE (-9.45%) — CFTC's June 10 proposed rule legitimising Polymarket/Kalshi prediction platforms stoked competition fears for CBOE's derivatives franchise; shares down ~28% over the month on the narrative. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe — CBOE is a large-cap exchange operator in diversified financials. The move is a weeks-long regulatory/competitive narrative, not a technical trigger any momentum or mean-reversion filter surfaces.

top_movers.catalyst: Piper Sandler reiterated Overweight with $280 target, citing proprietary data suggesting GTA VI (Nov 19, 2026 launch) could sell 45M+ units; FY27 net-bookings guidance of $8.0–$8.2B flagged as conservative.
top_movers.miss_reason: TTWO is outside all active strategy universes — large-cap gaming (~$18B mkt-cap) not covered by current scans. The move was triggered by an intraday sell-side reiteration; without real-time analyst-note ingestion, no strategy could react in time.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an analyst-catalyst signal: if a Tier-1 firm raises/reiterates target ≥12% above prior close on a name >$3B mkt-cap, queue for open-gap momentum entry requiring ≥1.5× 20-day avg volume within the first 15 min of regular trading.

top_movers.catalyst: Trump administration announced a Strait of Hormuz peace deal, restoring Europe–Asia flight corridors and cutting jet-fuel costs; the entire online travel sector rallied on geopolitical relief.
top_movers.miss_reason: ABNB is outside any active strategy's universe. The move was macro-driven — the Hormuz reopening lifted all travel names simultaneously; no single-name momentum or news-reactive signal can pre-position for a simultaneous sector-wide geopolitical shock.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a travel-macro vehicle (e.g. JETS ETF or an ABNB/BKNG/EXPE basket) to a geopolitical-catalyst strategy that enters when ≥2 OTA names gap ≥3% at open on confirmed route-restoration or peace-deal news.

top_movers.catalyst: FDA VRBPAC briefing docs for Moderna's mFlusiva mRNA flu vaccine found no major deficiencies ahead of June 18 adcom, reversing prior refuse-to-file concerns and signaling a viable Aug 5 approval path.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. MRNA is mid-cap biotech; the move came from FDA briefing docs released pre-market for a pre-scheduled adcom — a catalyst requiring pre-market positioning the bot cannot capture post-open.
top_movers.suggestion: Build a pre-adcom overlay: ingest the FDA advisory committee calendar, flag names where briefing docs publish with no-major-deficiency language the day before VRBPAC, and allow the news-reactive strategy a capped entry at the open.

top_movers.catalyst: Morgan Stanley raised WDC price target 33% to $650 on AI-HDD demand thesis (Jun 15), sparking a +16% then +7% move; today's +4.22% is third-day continuation of that analyst-upgrade re-rating.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. The catalyst was a multi-day analyst re-rating (Jun 15–16, +16% then +7%); by Jun 17 WDC was in high-RSI continuation mode and momentum filters requiring a fresh breakout would have screened it out.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a 'post-upgrade follow-through' rule: names with a ≥10% analyst-upgrade gap in the prior 2 sessions that hold above open-VWAP qualify for momentum entry with RSI ceiling lifted to 80 and a 1-day volume lookback instead of 5.

top_movers.catalyst: $2.75B debt tender offer (EUR refinancing for rate/FX savings) + multi-insider stock purchases (2 directors, CAO) reversed the June 15 CEO-departure selloff; new CEO Takis Georgakopoulos (internal, co-president merchant) seen as continuity.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe (large-cap fintech processor). The +4% was a mean-reversion recovery from a CEO-exit gap-down two days prior, catalyzed by insider-buy SEC filings and a corporate refinancing — no current filter surfaces post-shock insider-buy setups.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a catalyst-recovery scanner: names down ≥8% on a C-suite departure that subsequently show SEC Form 4 insider buys within 48 hrs become eligible for a 1-day mean-reversion entry at next open, capped at 0.5% NAV.

top_movers.catalyst: CFTC's June 10 proposed rule legitimising Polymarket/Kalshi prediction platforms stoked competition fears for CBOE's derivatives franchise; shares down ~28% over the month on the narrative.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — CBOE is a large-cap exchange operator in diversified financials. The move is a weeks-long regulatory/competitive narrative, not a technical trigger any momentum or mean-reversion filter surfaces.
top_movers.suggestion: (no actionable change — capturing this downside requires short capability the bot does not have; log CBOE as a sector-risk monitor and revisit if a long-side mean-reversion setup emerges near the 200-day MA.)

top_movers.catalyst: Sector-wide semiconductor de-rating following Broadcom's June 3 soft AI forward guidance (no full-year raise); rising Treasury yields from a strong May jobs report amplified risk-off selling in high-multiple chip names like MPWR.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. At ~$1,499/share with 59x forward P/E, MPWR likely fails price-per-share or valuation caps; the drop was pure sector contagion—no MPWR-specific news for a news-reactive strategy to trigger on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a SOX-contagion rule: when the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index drops >5% in a rolling 10-day window, flag semiconductor names with P/E >40x outside the current universe as short candidates for a 48-hour entry window.

top_movers.catalyst: Cluster of six analyst downgrades (Morgan Stanley, Wells Fargo, Barclays, Bernstein all cut to Underweight/Underperform June 11-12) triggered a valuation reset after INTC's ~250% 2026 AI-rally pushed it ~40% above the $87 consensus target.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — INTC is a $500B+ mega-cap semiconductor not in any configured universe. The 2-day cascade (-6.4% on June 16, -8.5% on June 17) was analyst-downgrade continuation, a signal type requiring event-driven coverage the current strategies lack.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a large-cap semi watchlist with a short-gate rule: ≥3 new Underweight/Underperform calls within 5 days AND price ≥30% above consensus activates a short signal for the next session (requires short capability to deploy).

top_movers.catalyst: Sector-wide profit-taking in AI photonics after LITE's ~140% YTD rally; no company-specific negative news — COHR and AAOI fell in tandem, consistent with valuation-stretch (~177x P/E) rotation.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. LITE (~$68B large-cap AI photonics, ~177x P/E, 52-wk range $84–$1,086) likely fails both valuation and volatility screens calibrated for more moderate regimes across all running strategies.
top_movers.suggestion: Add AI-photonics names (LITE, COHR, AAOI) to a momentum-reversal universe: short entry when RSI(14) > 80 AND 5-day gain > 15%; their stretched P/E (~177x) makes them prone to sharp mean-reversion on sector rotation days.
